why: B is only the porter Akkub of 1CH 9:17, which A already holds and names first in its line; 1CH 9:17 parallels NEH 11:19 (Akkub, Talmon at the gates), so nothing in B differs from A.
B covers NEH 11:19 and NEH 12:25, both already in A, and describes the same Levite porter beside Talmon; B is a thinner copy of A.

Both are the single Amaziah of 1CH 6:45, son of Hilkiah and father of Hashabiah, with identical ties. B also has the ties pointing back, and it reads the line correctly as Ethan the Merarite's (1CH 6:44-45), where A calls it Kohathite.

Both are Amos of LUK 3:25, son of Naum and father of Mattathias, with identical ties. A's MAT 1:10 is a wrong verse: there the Greek Amos is king Amon, son of Manasseh, and that verse should be dropped.

A is the family head whose descendants returned (EZR 2:5, NEH 7:10); B is the father of Shechaniah, Tobiah's father-in-law (NEH 6:18). 'Son of Arah' may mean a member of that family or a man's actual father, and the text does not say which.
B is Asaiah son of Haggiah in the Merarite line of 1CH 6:30, which A already holds with the same father and ties, and also identifies with the chief of Merari in 1CH 15:6.

A is the forefather of the 'children of Ater of Hezekiah' (EZR 2:16, NEH 7:21); B is the Ater who sealed the covenant about 90 years later (NEH 10:17). 'Ater, Hizkijah' may be the family signing under its name or a man of that name, and the text does not decide.

B is Azareel of the eleventh course (1CH 25:18), whom A's line and notes already name; the son of Heman (1CH 25:4) and A's 'Korahite' agree, since Heman descends from Korah. A's tie to the Ziklag Korhite of 1CH 12:6 is a separate, unproven link.

EZR 7:3 shortens the high-priestly line of 1CH 6:7-11, going from Azariah, father of the second Amariah, straight back to Meraioth. So the Azariah of EZR 7:3 is the one of 1CH 6:10-11, and A already holds EZR 7:3 with the same ties.

A is a leader who came up with Zerubbabel about 538 BC (EZR 2:2, NEH 7:7); B sealed Nehemiah's covenant about 445 BC (NEH 10:27). The two are about 90 years apart, so they are almost certainly different men, and A's note tying it to NEH 10:27 should go.
Both are the second-degree Levite with the psaltery in 1CH 15:18 and 15:20. B also carries 1CH 16:5 and the Levi and Eliab ties.

B is the forefather of the 1,254 'children of Elam' (EZR 2:7, NEH 7:12), which is exactly A's line; B is a thinner copy. A's NEH 12:42 (an Elam among the singers at the dedication) is a different man and should be dropped.

A is the forefather of the returning family (EZR 2:7); B is the Elam among the chiefs who sealed in NEH 10:14, about 90 years later. That list may give family names (Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam) or living men, and the text does not decide.
Both are Eliel, chief of the sons of Hebron with 80 brethren (1CH 15:9). A also has 1CH 15:11 and the tie back from Hebron.

Both are the priest Eliezer of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak who had a foreign wife (EZR 10:18). B's EZR 10:23 Eliezer is listed separately among the Levites and is another man, so that verse should come off it.
B is Elnathan of Jerusalem, father of Nehushta (2KI 24:8), which A already holds. A's link to Elnathan son of Achbor, Jehoiakim's official (JER 26:22, 36:12), fits the same generation.
B is only Ethan the Ezrahite of 1KI 4:31, which is A's line. A adds the 1CH 2:6 identification, which its notes argue.
Both are Ezer, father of Hushah, among the sons of Hur (1CH 4:4), with identical ties. A also has the tie back from Hushah.

Both are the Macedonian Gaius seized with Aristarchus at Ephesus (ACT 19:29), with identical ties. A's ROM 16:23, 1CO 1:14 and 3JN 1:1 are probably other men (Gaius of Corinth, the elder's friend) and should be reviewed.
B is Gera son of Bela (1CH 8:3), which A already holds. GEN 46:21 lists grandsons such as Ard and Naaman as Benjamin's sons (compare NUM 26:40), so A's identification with GEN 46:21 holds.
Both are Hananiah son of Shelemiah, who repaired the wall (NEH 3:30), with the same father. B's link to the sealer of NEH 10:23 is the same generation but unproven.

A is the forefather of the lay family Harim (EZR 2:32, NEH 7:35, EZR 10:31); B is the Harim among the chiefs who sealed in NEH 10:27, about 90 years after the return. Whether that is the family's name or a living man, the text does not decide.

A is the priestly house of Harim, from David's courses (1CH 24:8) through the return (EZR 2:39); B is the priest Harim who sealed in NEH 10:5. The priestly sealers mirror the house names of NEH 12:12-21, but whether NEH 10:5 names a house or a man, the text does not decide.

A is Hashabiah son of Bunni, a Merarite, father of Azrikam (1CH 9:14, NEH 11:15). B is at heart Hashabiah son of Jeduthun, of the twelfth lot in David's day (1CH 25:3, 25:19). Their fathers differ, so B's NEH 11:15 and its son-of-Bunni tie are wrong (as is its 1CH 26:30 Hebronite).

B is the priestly house head Iddo who came up with Zerubbabel (NEH 12:4), with Zechariah heading his house under Joiakim (NEH 12:16). A holds both verses, and the usual identification of that Zechariah with the prophet 'son of Iddo' (EZR 5:1, ZEC 1:1) makes them one.
Both are the priest Jarib of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak who had a foreign wife (EZR 10:18), with the same tie. A's added EZR 8:16 is the same year and plausible.
B is the priestly family 'Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua' (EZR 2:36, NEH 7:39), which A's line cites. A also merges the two separate Jedaiahs of NEH 12:6 and 12:7, which should be split.

A is only the overseer under Cononiah (2CH 31:13); B is at heart the Hemanite Jehiel who cleansed the temple (2CH 29:14), with 31:13 added. It is the same reign, and a Shimei stands beside him in both verses, but the text does not say they are one man.
Both are Jeiel of the sons of Elizaphan (2CH 29:13), with the same tie. B rightly calls him a Kohathite (Elizaphan son of Uzziel, EXO 6:22), where A's 'Gershonite' is wrong.

B is the priest who went up with Zerubbabel and whose house Hananiah led under Joiakim (NEH 12:1, 12:12). A holds both verses with the identical three ties. A's sealer (NEH 10:2) and procession (NEH 12:34) Jeremiahs are 90 years later and probably other men.
1CH 15:11 calls the chiefs just listed in 15:5-10 in order (Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, Amminadab), so its Joel is the Gershomite chief of 1CH 15:7, whom B holds with both verses.
Both are Joel, chief of the sons of Gershom with 130 brethren (1CH 15:7). B has that verse, its fuller Gershonite ties and the Laadan line.

A is Malluch of the sons of Bani with a foreign wife (EZR 10:29); B is the Malluch who sealed in NEH 10:27. EZR 10:32 has another Malluch, of the sons of Harim, and NEH 10:27 reads 'Malluch, Harim', so the text does not decide which Malluch, if either, sealed.
B is the priest who went up with Zerubbabel and whose house Jonathan led (NEH 12:2, 12:14), both held by A with the same Jonathan tie. A's link to the sealer of NEH 10:4 is a separate, unproven link.

A is Mattaniah son of Michaiah son of Zaccur, great-grandfather of the trumpeter Zechariah of 445 BC (NEH 12:35; compare NEH 11:17). B is at heart the Asaphite Mattaniah of Hezekiah's day (2CH 29:13), nearly three centuries earlier. B's NEH 12:35 and its son-of-Micaiah tie are wrong.
Both are the Meshullam on Ezra's left hand at the reading of the law (NEH 8:4), with no other verse. B has the tie to Ezra, and A's 'Levi' tribe is not stated there.

Both are Meshullam, head of the priestly house of Ezra under Joiakim (NEH 12:13). A has the tie back from ezra-3, but its own descendant-of tie points at Ezra the scribe and should be ezra-3, the priest of NEH 12:1, as B has it.

1CH 11:38 'Joel the brother of Nathan' holds the same place in the list of David's mighty men as 2SA 23:36 'Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah'. A holds both parallels; B's 'tribe of Judah' is unsupported.

A is Rehum son of Bani, who led the Levites' repairs (NEH 3:17). B seals among the lay 'chiefs of the people' (NEH 10:14-27, at 10:25), while the Levites sealed separately in NEH 10:9-13, so A's note claiming NEH 10:25 is wrong.

The Seraiah son of Azariah son of Hilkiah in Ezra's line (EZR 7:1) is the chief priest of 1CH 6:14 and 2KI 25:18, here as Ezra's ancestor. Both records give the same father and the tie to Ezra, and B is far fuller.
Both are Shaphan son of Azaliah son of Meshullam, Josiah's scribe who read the found book (2KI 22:3-14, 2CH 34:8-18). All of B's nine verses are in A's 23.

B is the trumpeter Zechariah's grandfather (NEH 12:35); A is at heart a chief man Ezra sent to Iddo (EZR 8:16), with NEH 12:35 attached. Nothing in either verse links the two, and A's father is wrongly the Hezekiah-era Mattaniah.

B is the priest who went up with Zerubbabel and whose house Jehonathan led (NEH 12:6, 12:18), both held by A with the same tie. A's NEH 12:34, 12:36 (a Levite musician) and 12:42 are other Shemaiahs and should be split off.
The 'sons of Shephatiah' who came with Ezra (EZR 8:8) are the same family as in EZR 2:4 and NEH 7:9: EZR 8 lists the return families of EZR 2 again. B holds all three verses and the ties.

1CH 4:1 is a descending line (Pharez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, Shobal), so its Shobal is Hur's son of 1CH 2:50, father of Reaiah (4:2, 'Haroeh' in 2:52). A holds all four verses; B's 'son of Judah' misreads 4:1.

Tahath son of Assir son of Ebiasaph son of Korah (1CH 6:37) is the Tahath of the Kohathite line in 1CH 6:22-24, with the same father. A holds both verses, and the two sons (Uriel, Zephaniah) are different branches from one Tahath.
B is Timna, Lotan's sister (GEN 36:22, 1CH 1:39), which A holds. A's further identification with Eliphaz's concubine (GEN 36:12) is traditional, not stated, and worth a note.
Both are Uriel son of Tahath and father of Uzziah (1CH 6:24), with identical ties. A adds 1CH 6:36 and the chief of Kohath (1CH 15:5, 15:11).
B is Zaccur son of Mattaniah, father of Hanan the treasurer (NEH 13:13), with exactly A's ties. A's link to the Levite sealer Zaccur (NEH 10:12) is the same generation but unproven.

A is Zadok son of Baana, who repaired the wall (NEH 3:4); B is a Zadok among the lay chiefs who sealed (NEH 10:21) in the same years. NEH 3:29 has another Zadok, son of Immer, so the text does not say which one, if either, sealed.
